# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 19 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 19 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_019_page_001.jpg

---

## Vision 3, Chapter 11

**1** He began to explain: "Listen carefully and take all this in. The stones from the plain that were placed in the building — the square, white, perfectly-fitting ones — those are the apostles, bishops, teachers, and deacons who lived in God's holiness and served faithfully and purely in their roles. Some have died; others are still living. They were always in harmony with each other, lived at peace, and truly listened to one another. That's why they fit so seamlessly into the tower." **2** "Those hauled up from the deep sea — those are the ones who suffered and gave their lives for the name of the Lord." **3** "Those brought from the mountains are the long-standing believers — not new converts, but people whose faithfulness has been proven across a whole lifetime, who are honored in the community of God's people." **4** "But those from the first mountain — the black one — those are apostates. Church-betrayers. People who blasphemed the Lord through their sinning and are ashamed of the name of the Lord. These people are spiritually dead. They have no place in the building — they're useless." **5** "Those from the second mountain — the bare one — those are hypocrites and teachers of evil, people who corrupt other believers, especially the more vulnerable ones. They're beyond repentance, and their mouths are still full of blasphemy. They might barely count as stones — but only barely."

---

*PNEUMA note: The stark "spiritually dead" and "useless" language for the first mountain reflects the Shepherd's unsentimental realism about apostasy — there are some conditions that place people beyond the tower.*
